jonah.4.p1.b1.text: Jonah, however, was greatly displeased, and he became angry.

jonah.4.p1.b2.text: “O LORD … I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion—One who relents from sending disaster.

jonah.4.p1.b3.text: This is why I was so quick to flee toward Tarshish.

jonah.4.p1.b4.text: And now, O LORD, please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.”

jonah.4.p2.b1.text: “Have you any right to be angry?”

jonah.4.p2.b2.text: Then Jonah left the city and sat down east of it

jonah.4.p2.b3.text: where he made himself a shelter and sat in its shade to see what would happen to the city.

jonah.4.p3.b1.text: So the LORD God appointed a vine, and it grew up to provide shade over Jonah’s head to ease his discomfort

jonah.4.p3.b2.text: Jonah was greatly pleased with the plant.

jonah.4.p4.b1.text: When dawn came the next day, God appointed a worm that attacked the plant so that it withered.

jonah.4.p4.b2.text: As the sun was rising, God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah’s head so that he grew faint

jonah.4.p4.b3.text: and wished to die, saying, “It is better for me to die than to live.”

jonah.4.p4.b4.text: “Have you any right to be angry about the plant?”

jonah.4.p5.b1.text: “You cared about the plant, which you neither tended nor made grow. It sprang up in a night and perished in a night.

jonah.4.p5.b2.text: So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh, which has more than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left
